ModuleName: HCI Design Documentation and Development Reporting
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Outlines the module's core topics—covering HCI development reporting, requirements documentation, design process documentation, and evaluation documentation—giving learners and instructors a structured overview of what will be taught and in what order.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: A navigational overview of the module's topics—covering the purpose of HCI development reports, design decision traceability, and professional documentation standards—that learners use to preview and access the module's subject areas before engaging with detailed content.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to HCI Development Reporting
Artifacts.Description: Introduces what an HCI Development Report is, why it differs from informal documentation, and how learners should approach creating a formal structured record of their design project from user needs through to prototype evaluation.

Artifacts.Name: Requirements Documentation
Artifacts.Description: Explains how to capture and document user needs, functional and non-functional requirements, and design constraints, giving learners a guide to building the research and planning foundation that underpins all subsequent design decisions.

Artifacts.Name: Design Process Documentation
Artifacts.Description: Covers how to record design decisions, experiments, and iterative changes throughout a project, helping learners create a transparent, evidence-based account of how and why their design evolved over time.

Artifacts.Name: Evaluation Documentation
Artifacts.Description: Describes how to formally document usability evaluations, including methods used, findings gathered, and how results influenced design revisions, enabling learners to demonstrate that their design choices were grounded in observed user behaviour.

Artifacts.Name: Final Implementation Documentation
Artifacts.Description: Explains how to write the closing section of an HCI project report by documenting what was built, how faithfully it reflects earlier design intentions, and honestly accounting for any gaps between planned and delivered outcomes.

Artifacts.Name: Group Collaboration and Contribution Documentation
Artifacts.Description: Covers how to record team members' individual contributions, collaborative processes, decision-making, and reflections in group projects, helping learners and instructors assess both collective output and each person's role.

Artifacts.Name: Report Structure, Referencing, and Presentation
Artifacts.Description: Guides learners on how to organise a professional HCI report with a coherent structure, apply correct academic referencing, and present the document to communicate a clear, evidence-backed design narrative to evaluators.
